panels.shot: epic twilight wide of a royal campaign tent glowing in a dusty camp, low-angle
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri sits stern yet calm at the entrance of his great tent, armed Afghan officers frozen behind him, while weary peasants and traders stand hesitantly before the king in the fading light of a battlefield camp.

dialogue.text: In Sher Shah Suri’s war-torn age, the king’s battlefield tent becomes a court of justice—where a peasant may accuse a soldier, and the ruler’s mercy stands beside his power.

i18n.hi: शेर शाह सूरी के जंग भरे दौर में, मैदान का बादशाही तम्बू अदालत बन जाता है—जहाँ किसान सिपाही पर एलान करता है, और रहमत ताकत के साथ खड़ी रहती है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high bird’s-eye over North India, roads and rivers sketched across plains
panels.action: A stylized map of Sher Shah’s dominions stretches from the Ganga plains toward Punjab and the Indus, with new caravan roads and serais marked like arteries, as Sher Shah Suri’s profile overlaps the landscape.

dialogue.text: By the early 1540s, Sher Shah’s rule runs from Delhi to Bihar and towards Punjab, bound together by roads, serais and revenue officers—but power means little if the weak cannot find justice.

i18n.hi: १५४० के शुरू होते ही, शेर शाह की हुकूमत दिल्ली से बिहार, पंजाब की तरफ तक फैली है—सड़कें, सरायें, कारिंदों से बंधी; पर अगर कमजोर को इंसाफ न मिले, तो ये ताकत खोखली है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of the royal camp tent, lit by oil lamps, with Afghan nobles seated
panels.action: Inside the king’s tent, Sher Shah Suri sits on a simple raised seat, robes plain but clean, Afghan chiefs and clerks arranged around him, as villagers and merchants cluster at the entrance waiting.

dialogue.text: Abbas Khan Sarwani will later praise him: a ruler who hears petitions in camp and court, rebukes his own Afghans, and speaks of the oppressed as complainants before God.

i18n.hi: अब्बास ख़ान सरवानी बाद में उसे यूँ सराहेगा: ऐसा बादशाह, जो लश्कर और दरबार दोनों में अर्ज़ सुनता है, अपने अफ़गानों को डाँटता है, और मज़लूम को खुदा के सामने फ़रियादी कहता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Sher Shah’s face, stern eyes softened with attentiveness
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri leans forward slightly, brows furrowed, listening intently to an unseen petitioner beyond the frame, a scribe at his side poised with reed pen over paper.

dialogue.text: Indo-Persian ideals of kingship demand more than conquest: the just sultan must be a shadow of divine order, hearing the cry of the weak wherever his standard stands.

i18n.hi: हिंद–फ़ारसी तसव्वुर में बादशाहत सिर्फ फ़तह नहीं माँगती: आदिल सुल्तान खुदा के निज़ाम का साया बने, जहाँ भी उसका अलम गड़े, वहाँ कमजोर की चीख सुने।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot at tent entrance, a peasant steps forward toward the throne
panels.action: A barefoot cultivator in coarse cotton stands in the foreground, hands raised in supplication, while Sher Shah Suri watches from his seat, nobles murmuring at the peasant’s boldness.

dialogue.text: Sarwani’s stories show cultivators and traders walking into this tent of kings, naming the very officers who wronged them—and living to be heard.

i18n.hi: सरवानी की दास्तानें दिखाती हैं: खेतीहर, सौदागर इस बादशाही तम्बू में चले आते हैं, जालिम अफ़सरों के नाम लेके शिकायत करते हैं—और जान बचाकर सुनाए जाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot with a burly Afghan soldier kneeling, guarded by other troops behind
panels.action: A broad-shouldered Afghan soldier kneels with restrained hands, eyes lowered, guarded by grim comrades, while Sher Shah Suri points toward him in cool reprimand.

dialogue.text: In one oft-retold pattern, an Afghan commander seizes a peasant’s land or extorts a trader; the complaint reaches the king, and the officer is disgraced or dismissed.

i18n.hi: अक्सर सुनाई जाने वाली एक मिसाल में, अफ़गान सरदार किसी किसान की ज़मीन हड़पता है या सौदागर को निचोड़ता है; बात बादशाह तक पहुँचती है, और वो सरदार रुसवा या बरखास्त होता है।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Sher Shah rising from his seat, hand raised in admonition
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri rises halfway from his seat, one hand lifted in a measured gesture of warning toward his assembled officers, lamp-light sharpening the lines of his face.

dialogue.speaker: sher_shah_suri
dialogue.text: He who oppresses my subjects opposes God, and I will not shield him.

i18n.hi: जो मेरे रइयों पर ज़ुल्म करे, वो खुदा से बैर ले—मैं उसे आड़ नहीं दूँगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a busy highway with serais, watchmen and distant hills
panels.action: A grand road cuts across the frame, travellers on foot and horseback moving between fortified serais, while watchmen stand at intervals and fields stretch away toward village clusters.

dialogue.text: Sher Shah’s new roads and serais promise safe passage from Bengal to the Indus—but every fresh path also invites robbery and abuse unless someone is made answerable.

i18n.hi: शेर शाह की नई सड़कें और सरायें बंगाल से सिंधु तक महफ़ूज़ सफ़र का वादा करती हैं—पर हर ताज़ा राह डाकू और ज़्यादती भी बुलाती है, अगर कोई जवाबदेह न ठहराया जाए।

panels.shot: medium shot at a village edge, headmen assembled before a royal officer with decree
panels.action: Under a peepal tree by the roadside, village headmen stand in a tense line as a royal official reads out orders from a scroll, gesturing toward the highway and a nearby milestone.

dialogue.text: Sarwani records a harsher rule beneath the promise: if a traveller is robbed or killed near a settlement, the village headmen will answer with fines or worse.

i18n.hi: सरवानी इस वादे के नीचे सख्त क़ानून भी दर्ज करता है: अगर मुसाफिर बस्ती के आस–पास लुटे या मारा जाए, तो गाँव के मुकद्दमों से जुरमाना ही नहीं, सज़ा भी ली जाए।

panels.shot: interior medium shot in tent, Sher Shah listening to a merchant describe an ambush
panels.action: A weary trader with dust-streaked face and travel-worn clothes gestures anxiously, describing an unseen attack, while Sher Shah Suri listens, chin resting lightly on his hand.

dialogue.text: A merchant robbed on Sher Shah’s highway can appeal straight to the king; the story traces from road to pargana office to the village elder whose negligence is blamed.

i18n.hi: शेर शाह की सड़क पर लुटे हुए सौदागर को सीधी बादशाह तक गुहार का हक है; किस्सा सड़क से परगना दफ़्तर तक, फिर उस गाँव के बुज़ुर्ग तक जाता है, जिसकी लापरवाही पर इलज़ाम ठहरता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sher Shah conferring with scribes and qazis over ledgers and reports
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri sits surrounded by thick ledgers and folded farmans, conferring with a qazi and a revenue official who point to written reports of road incidents and village liabilities.

dialogue.text: Behind each anecdote lies a system: reports from highway posts, village fines entered into revenue records, and qazis and officials tying justice to the king’s communications network.

i18n.hi: हर हक़ायत के पीछे एक निज़ाम छिपा है: राहगुज़रों से रिपोर्ट, गाँवों पर जुर्माने राजस्व दफ्तरों में दर्ज, और क़ाज़ी–अमले जो बादशाह की इत्तलाआँ की रगों से न्याय बाँधते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a village assembly, elder kneeling as guards watch and villagers look on
panels.action: In a village square, the headman kneels with tense composure before a visiting royal officer, flanked by armed guards, while villagers watch in anxious silence from doorways.

dialogue.text: Collective responsibility forces local elites to police their own surroundings; it brings quick order to roads, but also spreads fear, as one man’s crime becomes the village’s burden.

i18n.hi: बाहमी ज़िम्मेदारी से इलाक़े के अमीर खुद अपने इर्द–गिर्द निगरानी को मजबूर होते हैं; सड़कों पर जल्दी अमन आता है, पर खौफ़ भी फैलता है—एक की ख़ता पूरे गाँव का बोझ बन जाती है।

panels.shot: moody interior shot of tent at night, Sher Shah alone, map and sword beside him
panels.action: At night inside the tent, Sher Shah Suri sits alone with a map and a sheathed sword beside him, his face lit by a single lamp as he gazes outward, deep in thought.

dialogue.text: For later writers, he becomes almost a saint of justice. Yet even Sarwani’s praise cannot hide the steel: his compassion travels with coercion in the same saddlebag.

i18n.hi: बाद के नस्ख़ों में वो जैसे इंसाफ़ का बुज़ुर्ग बन जाता है। पर सरवानी की तारीफ़ भी उसकी फौलाद नीयत नहीं छुपा पाती: नर्मी और सख्ती एक ही रकाब में सफ़र करती हैं।

panels.shot: solemn medium shot recalling a siege: distant fort of Raisen under smoky sky
panels.action: A memory-like tableau shows the hill fort of Raisen under a hazy, smoke-streaked sky, Afghan siege lines encircling it, banners snapping in the wind beyond the trenches.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere in this chapter stands Raisen, where Sher Shah’s siege ends in grim surrender and deaths; the same king who protects traders also compels Rajput forts to bow or break.

i18n.hi: यहीं इस बाब में रैसिन भी है, जहाँ शेर शाह का घेराव खौफ़नाक सरेंडर और मौतों पर खत्म होता है; वही बादशाह जो सौदागरों को बचाता है, राजपूत क़िलों को झुकने या टूटने पर भी मजबूर करता है।

panels.shot: medium shot back in the tent, contrasting nobles on one side and common petitioners on other
panels.action: Inside the tent, Afghan nobles sit in ordered ranks on one side, while peasants and merchants cluster on the other, Sher Shah Suri at the center, weighing their opposing claims.

dialogue.text: Justice at the king’s tent is never neutral ground: it balances the sword-bearing elite against tax-paying subjects, and every decision tightens or loosens that fragile bond.

i18n.hi: राजा के तम्बू का न्याय कभी बेपक्ष नहीं होता: तलवार वाली जमात और लगान देने वाले रइया के बीच तौल चलता है—हर फ़ैसला इस नाज़ुक रिश्ते को ढीला या कसा करता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Sher Shah’s camp court, officers standing chastened as a peasant departs relieved
panels.action: A peasant walks away from the king’s tent with a calmer stride, while a previously accused officer stands apart, chastened, under the watchful eyes of Sher Shah Suri seated in composed authority.

dialogue.text: For Abu’l-Fazl, writing later, real kingship demands such accountability: officers answer for abuses, roads are guarded, and royal authority rests on the trust of those who travel and sow.

i18n.hi: अबुल–फ़ज़ल के लिए, जो बाद में लिखता है, असली बादशाहत ऐसी जवाबदेही माँगती है: अफ़सर ज़ुल्म पर कटघरे में आते हैं, सड़कें मुहाफ़िजों से चलती हैं, और ताज की ताकत रस्तों और खेतों पर भरोसे पर टिकी होती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Sher Shah’s weathered hands resting on his knee, ring glinting softly
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri’s hands rest firm on his knee, a plain signet ring catching lamplight, his posture steady as if bearing the weight of distant villages and roads

dialogue.text: Sher Shah’s justice tales are shaped by loyal chroniclers, but they reveal a hard lesson: power that travels in roads must also travel in responsibility—or it becomes only display.

i18n.hi: शेर शाह के इंसाफ़ के किस्से वफ़ादार मुहद्दिसों से सँवरकर आते हैं, पर उनमें सख्त सबक छुपा है: जो ताकत सड़कों पर सफ़र करे, उसे ज़िम्मेदारी भी साथ लेनी होगी—वरना वो सिर्फ दिखावा रह जाएगी।
